title: Align retry classifier + backoff defaults with cross-SDK spec; add custom policy hooks + per-request overrides
author: Dana Lo
body:
Context: As part of the SDK parity audit, we are standardizing retry behavior across Python/TS/Go to reduce support load and eliminate inconsistent client behavior (see ENG-2482 / ENG-2487, ADR-0137 draft). This PR updates the TypeScript SDK retry classifier + backoff defaults to match the cross-SDK spec and adds explicit hooks for custom retry policies and per-request overrides.

What changed: 1) Retry classifier parity: retry on HTTP 429, 500, 502, 503, 504; do not retry on 4xx (other than 429) including 401/403; treat network/transport errors as retryable when request is replayable (e.g., fetch/undici errors like ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, EPIPE, ENOTFOUND). 2) Backoff/jitter defaults: exponential backoff with full jitter; base delay 250ms, cap 4s; honor Retry-After (seconds or HTTP date) when present on 429/503, but cap to 30s to avoid unbounded client stall. 3) Retry budget: default maxRetries=2 (3 total attempts) with a per-request override; we also expose a lightweight budget hook so callers can implement their own global budget/circuiting if desired. 4) Opt-outs + per-request overrides: callers can set retry: false, retry: { maxRetries }, or retry: { shouldRetry } on a per-request basis; constructor-level defaults remain available via new RetryPolicy plumbing. 5) Telemetry hooks: add onRetry callback invoked with attempt number, delay, status code (if any), request-id (if available), and error classification (rate_limit/server_error/transport). The hook is intentionally non-logging and does not include auth headers.

Notes/constraints: - We do not retry streaming requests after the response body has started; mid-stream disconnect behavior is handled in the streaming PR (PR-289). - We only retry when the request body is known-replayable; for JSON requests (the common path) we can safely re-send. For arbitrary ReadableStream bodies, we do not retry and surface the error. - This PR does not change server-side behavior; it relies on gateway headers like request-id / retry-after where available.

Testing: added unit tests covering (a) 429 with Retry-After, (b) 503 flap, (c) transport error retry, (d) non-retryable 401/403/422, (e) per-request overrides and retry:false, and (f) callback invocation. Also verified via local repro against the throttling scenario reported in SUP-9334 (previous behavior caused prolonged throttling due to aggressive retries).

Rollout/compat: This is intended as a non-breaking behavior change. However, customers who depended on the previous default (higher retry count) may see fewer total attempts; the new defaults match the cross-SDK spec and SRE guidance to reduce retry amplification during incidents. Docs update will follow in the docs PR for parity.

Refs: ENG-2482, ENG-2487, SUP-9334, ADR-0137 (retry policy unification), API Gateway guidance on request-id and Retry-After.
commits: sdk(retry): add RetryPolicy interface + default implementation
sdk(retry): align retryable status codes and transport error mapping
sdk(retry): implement exponential backoff w/ full jitter + Retry-After support
sdk(client): add per-request retry overrides and disable path
docs(inline): update JSDoc for retry options + examples
changed_areas: packages/sdk/test/retry.test.ts (new matrix tests w/ mocked responses)
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan: Can you confirm defaults match the spec (2 retries, full jitter, cap 4s) and that we’re honoring Retry-After for 429? Also want to ensure we don’t retry streaming calls here.

Dana Lo (author): Confirmed: default maxRetries=2 (3 total attempts). Backoff uses full jitter with base 250ms and cap 4s; Retry-After is honored (seconds/date), with a 30s cap. Streaming is excluded (we only apply to non-streaming request path); streaming disconnect handling is in PR-289.

Rafael Mendes: Please avoid retry amplification: make sure retries stop on 4xx other than 429, and consider guarding against non-replayable bodies (ReadableStream). Also can we expose an onRetry hook for client-side metrics?

Dana Lo (author): Addressed in 8c2f1b4: classifier retries only 429/5xx + transport errors. Non-replayable bodies are detected; if body is a ReadableStream we mark it non-retryable and surface immediately. Added onRetry hook with attempt/delay/classification/request-id (no headers).
Amara Diallo: Gateway will always return request-id; Retry-After is guaranteed for 429 but not for 503. Please make sure we don’t fail if Retry-After is malformed and that we cap long delays.
Dana Lo (author): Added parsing hardening + fallback to backoff if Retry-After is malformed. Implemented delay cap of 30s and documented this in JSDoc.
Brian Murphy: Minor API ergonomics: can we allow per-request retry: false and retry: { maxRetries } without forcing a full policy object? Also update error messages to include retry exhaustion info.
Dana Lo (author): Implemented per-request retry shorthand (boolean | object). Retry exhaustion errors now include attempts + last status when applicable; telemetry hook also fires with final attempt.
Ibrahim Khan: Approved once changelog entry is added and tests cover 401/403 non-retry case.
Dana Lo (author): Added changelog entry + tests for 401/403/422 non-retry. Pushing final commit.
Rafael Mendes: Approved. Thanks for adding the replayable-body guard; that’s important for safety.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK: Retry defaults now match the cross-SDK standard (retry 429/5xx + transport errors; exponential backoff w/ jitter; default 2 retries).
TypeScript SDK: Added RetryPolicy hooks and per-request retry overrides (including retry:false) plus an onRetry callback for instrumentation.
TypeScript SDK: Improved handling of Retry-After on 429 and added parsing hardening.
